title: Cliff Jackson's eighteen-piece band
summary: From a photograph, Cliff led and arranged for a big band of about eighteen pieces; no recordings known.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Cliff never talked too much about himself and, you know, he had such a background, he had done so many things. There are probably a lot of his friends and people out there that know a whole lot more about Cliff than I do. I don't get a chance to come in contact with too many of the musicians that worked with Cliff who can give me

some ideas, you know, about what Cliff might have talked about or how he was in those days, but the only thing that I can get from them, everybody loved Cliff, you know, and he had a lot of patience. He told me that one of the reasons that he gave up the band was because he had a hard time to keep these guys together and it's a big headache, you know, seeing that they get to work on time.
How big a group was it?
Well, from the photograph that I have, he had about an 18-piece band.

And he did the arrangements and conducted the band, too. So this must have gone on about -- well, I have one photograph that was taken at a club, the Happy (i.e. Roane's) Club in 1926 and the other one is 1930, so he must have had the band for about four years, and that's a lot of headaches, you know, if you're having problems with the musicians and it's a lot of work.
Well, that's certainly a bigger group than Fletcher Henderson was leading at

Yes, he had a very big orchestra and he made the arrangements and conducted the band, rehearsed the band. It was a lot of work. He said he was younger then and he had more ambition but when he gave it up, he gave it up completely and the only writing he did was I guess whatever he did in Joe Davis's office.
I wonder if that's on record.
I doubt it, I doubt it, there are some recordings of Cliff with a small combination.
With his Krazy Kats but I doubt very much if the big band ever got on records.
Do you have any knowledge second hand of the style that they played?
I have no idea, I really don't. Chet's father played the tuba.
